lessons.explanation: Watch the vowel: responsible → responsable. comfortable is confortable, with an n.
lessons.speakingPrompt: Say each French word without looking. Then compare it with the model voice.

items.note: Same form for masculine and feminine: un horaire flexible, une règle flexible. The final e is silent in speech.
Same form for both genders. The s sounds like z and the final -ble is a soft, short sound: vee-ZEE-bluh.
Same form for both genders. Note -able, not -ible. As a noun, un responsable, une responsable means a manager.

lessons.title: -ist → -iste · People and -ist words · 2
lessons.objective: Add -e. The same form is used for men and women: un artiste, une artiste.
lessons.explanation: Use the pattern as a clue; check each French word and its meaning.
lessons.speakingPrompt: Say each French word without looking. Then compare it with the model voice.

items.note: Masculine and feminine: un optimiste, une optimiste. Also an adjective. The final e is silent: op-tee-MEEST.
Masculine and feminine: un pessimiste, une pessimiste. Double s, said as s: peh-see-MEEST.
Masculine and feminine: un spécialiste, une spécialiste. The sp- stays, with no é- in front. Say spay-sya-LEEST.

lessons.title: -ism → -isme · Ideas and movements · 2
lessons.objective: Add -e: tourism → tourisme. Masculine nouns: le tourisme.
lessons.explanation: Use the pattern as a clue; check each French word and its meaning.
lessons.speakingPrompt: Say each French word without looking. Then compare it with the model voice.

items.note: Masculine: le capitalisme. All -isme nouns are masculine. The final e is silent: ka-pee-ta-LEESM.
Masculine: le communisme. Double m, as in English. Say ko-mew-NEESM.
Masculine: le racisme. The c is a soft s: ra-SEESM. The adjective is raciste.

lessons.title: -ic → -ique · Adjectives in -ic · 2
lessons.objective: -ic becomes -ique, one form for masculine and feminine: électrique, fantastique. Watch public: feminine publique.
lessons.explanation: Nouns often end in -ique too: music → la musique, politics → la politique.
lessons.speakingPrompt: Say each French word without looking. Then compare it with the model voice.

items.note: Same form for both genders: un dîner romantique, une soirée romantique. The qu sounds like k: ro-mahn-TEEK.
Same form for both genders. It also means economical, cheap to run: une voiture économique.
Same form for both genders. Say spay-see-FEEK, with the stress on the last syllable.

lessons.title: -ical → -ique · Adjectives in -ical · 2
lessons.objective: -ical usually becomes -ique as well: practical → pratique, logical → logique.
lessons.explanation: A few keep -al: médical, musical, tropical, vertical.
lessons.speakingPrompt: Say each French word without looking. Then compare it with the model voice.

items.note: Same form for both genders: un événement historique. The h is silent: ees-to-REEK.
Same form for both genders. La logique is also the noun logic. The g before i is soft, like zh: lo-ZHEEK.
Same form for both genders: un plat typique. The y sounds like ee: tee-PEEK.

lessons.title: -al → -al · Adjectives in -al · 2
lessons.objective: Many are identical: normal, animal, final, local. The masculine plural usually ends in -aux: normaux, animaux.
lessons.explanation: actual is a false friend: actuel means current; actually is en fait.
lessons.speakingPrompt: Say each French word without looking. Then compare it with the model voice.

items.note: Feminine: générale; masculine plural: généraux. En général means in general. Say zhay-nay-RAL.
Masculine: l'hôpital; plural les hôpitaux. The circumflex replaces the s of hospital, and the h is silent.
Feminine: spéciale; masculine plural: spéciaux. Say spay-SYAL. Une offre spéciale is a special offer.

lessons.title: -ive → -if · Adjectives in -ive · 2
lessons.objective: -ive becomes -if in the masculine and stays -ive in the feminine: active → actif, active.
lessons.explanation: Use the pattern as a clue; check each French word and its meaning.
lessons.speakingPrompt: Say each French word without looking. Then compare it with the model voice.

items.note: Feminine: négative. The g is hard, as in game, and the final f is pronounced: nay-gah-TEEF.
Feminine: attractive. Used for prices and offers; an attractive person is attirant, attirante.
Feminine: excessive. The x sounds like ks and the final f is pronounced: ek-seh-SEEF.

lessons.title: -ous → -eux · Adjectives in -ous · 2
lessons.objective: -ous becomes -eux: curious → curieux. Feminine is -euse: curieuse.
lessons.explanation: A few change completely: famous → célèbre, various → divers. fameux exists, but it usually means well-known or, in speech, great.
lessons.speakingPrompt: Say each French word without looking. Then compare it with the model voice.

items.note: Feminine: généreuse. The final x is silent; -eux is the rounded vowel of deux.
Feminine: nerveuse. The final x is silent, and the r is at the back of the throat.
Feminine: mystérieuse. The y sounds like ee: mees-tay-RYUH; the final x is silent.

lessons.title: -ant / -ent → -ant / -ent · Adjectives and people in -ant / -ent · 2
lessons.objective: Often identical: important, intelligent. Add -e for the feminine: importante. Many also name people: un étudiant, une étudiante, le président.
lessons.explanation: Watch the spelling: different → différent, student → étudiant. The final t is silent in the masculine and heard in the feminine.
lessons.speakingPrompt: Say each French word without looking. Then compare it with the model voice.

items.note: Feminine: intelligente. The final t is silent in the masculine and heard in the feminine; g before e sounds like zh.
Feminine: patiente. Also a noun: le patient, la patiente. The final t is silent: pa-SYAHN.
Masculine: le président; feminine: la présidente. The final t is silent, and the ending is a nasal like dahn.

lessons.title: -ence → -ence · Nouns in -ence · 2
lessons.objective: -ence stays -ence, and the noun is feminine: la science, l'expérience.
lessons.explanation: l'expérience also means an experiment. une conférence is a talk or lecture; a big conference is un congrès. Exception: le silence is masculine.
lessons.speakingPrompt: Say each French word without looking. Then compare it with the model voice.

items.note: Feminine: la science. The sc before i sounds like s: SYAHNSS, with a nasal en.
Feminine: la présence. The ending -ence sounds like AHNSS, never like English ens.
Feminine: la violence. The ending is nasal, -AHNSS, and the final e is silent.

lessons.title: -ance → -ance · Nouns in -ance · 2
lessons.objective: -ance stays -ance, feminine: l'importance, la distance.
lessons.explanation: Use the pattern as a clue; check each French word and its meaning.
lessons.speakingPrompt: Say each French word without looking. Then compare it with the model voice.

items.note: Feminine: l'élégance. The g is hard before a, as in go: ay-lay-GAHNSS.
Feminine: la substance. The b sounds like p before the s, and the ending is nasal: sup-STAHNSS.
Feminine: la tolérance. One accented é, then a nasal ending: toh-lay-RAHNSS.

lessons.title: -ary → -aire · Nouns and adjectives in -ary · 2
lessons.objective: -ary becomes -aire: vocabulary → vocabulaire, necessary → nécessaire.
lessons.explanation: library is a false friend: la bibliothèque. Une librairie is a bookshop.
lessons.speakingPrompt: Say each French word without looking. Then compare it with the model voice.

items.note: Masculine or feminine: le secrétaire, la secrétaire. Only the second e takes an accent; -aire rhymes with air: suh-kray-TEHR.
Masculine: le salaire, even though it ends in -e. -aire rhymes with air.
Masculine: le dictionnaire. Double n, so the o is not nasal: deek-syo-NEHR. -aire rhymes with air.

lessons.title: -ize → -iser · Verbs in -ize · 2
lessons.objective: -ize becomes -iser: organize → organiser. They conjugate like any regular -er verb.
lessons.explanation: réaliser means to carry out or to make (a project, a film). To realize (understand) is se rendre compte.
lessons.speakingPrompt: Say each French word without looking. Then compare it with the model voice.

items.note: je mémorise, nous mémorisons. The s between vowels sounds like z; the infinitive ends in the sound ay.
je modernise, nous modernisons. The s sounds like z, and the final -er is pronounced ay.
je légalise, nous légalisons. The s sounds like z; the infinitive ends in the sound ay.

lessons.title: -ate → -er · Verbs in -ate · 2
lessons.objective: Replace -ate with -er: celebrate → célébrer, separate → séparer.
lessons.explanation: Use the pattern as a clue; check each French word and its meaning.
lessons.speakingPrompt: Say each French word without looking. Then compare it with the model voice.

items.note: je crée, nous créons. Two vowels in a row: kray-AY. The ending is the sound ay.
j'éduque, nous éduquons. The qu sounds like k. It means to bring up a child; to teach a subject is enseigner.
je décore, nous décorons. It can also mean to award a medal; the infinitive ends in the sound ay.

lessons.title: -ify → -ifier · Verbs in -ify · 2
lessons.objective: -ify becomes -ifier: identify → identifier.
lessons.explanation: Use the pattern as a clue; check each French word and its meaning.
lessons.speakingPrompt: Say each French word without looking. Then compare it with the model voice.

items.note: je justifie, nous justifions. The j sounds like zh; the infinitive ends in the sound yay.
je classifie, nous classifions. For to sort things into groups, classer is the common everyday verb.
je modifie, nous modifions. The infinitive ends in the sound fyay.

lessons.title: -ct → -ct · Words in -ct · 2
lessons.objective: Often identical: direct, correct, exact. Add -e for the feminine: directe.
lessons.explanation: Several drop the c: perfect → parfait, fact → le fait, product → le produit, effect → l'effet. In respect and aspect the final ct is silent.
lessons.speakingPrompt: Say each French word without looking. Then compare it with the model voice.

items.note: Masculine: le contact. The final ct is pronounced here: kohn-TAKT, with a nasal on.
Masculine: l'impact. The ct is pronounced: an-PAKT, with a nasal in.
Masculine: l'aspect. The final ct is silent: ass-PEH.

lessons.title: -ology → -ologie · Fields of study · 2
lessons.objective: -ology becomes -ologie, and the noun is feminine: biology → la biologie.
lessons.explanation: Use the pattern as a clue; check each French word and its meaning.
lessons.speakingPrompt: Say each French word without looking. Then compare it with the model voice.

items.note: Feminine: la géologie. The g sounds like zh, and the ending -gie sounds like zhee: zhay-oh-loh-ZHEE.
Feminine: l'écologie. The ending sounds like loh-ZHEE; an environmentalist is un écologiste.
Feminine: la sociologie. The c sounds like s: soh-syoh-loh-ZHEE.

lessons.title: -ologist → -ologue · Specialists in a field · 2
lessons.objective: -ologist becomes -ologue, one form for men and women: psychologist → un psychologue, une psychologue.
lessons.explanation: biologist is the exception: biologiste. An écologiste is an environmental activist, not a scientist.
lessons.speakingPrompt: Say each French word without looking. Then compare it with the model voice.

items.note: Masculine or feminine: le sociologue, la sociologue. The gu is a hard g, as in go; the u is silent.
Masculine or feminine: le cardiologue, la cardiologue. The gu is a hard g; the ending sounds like -LOG.
Masculine or feminine: l'archéologue. The ch sounds like k, as in other Greek words: ar-kay-oh-LOG.

lessons.title: -graphy → -graphie · Writing and recording words · 2
lessons.objective: -graphy becomes -graphie, and French keeps the ph: photography → la photographie. The nouns are feminine.
lessons.explanation: Use the pattern as a clue; check each French word and its meaning.
lessons.speakingPrompt: Say each French word without looking. Then compare it with the model voice.

items.note: Feminine: la chorégraphie. The ch sounds like k and ph like f: koh-ray-grah-FEE.
Feminine: la calligraphie. Double l; the ph sounds like f: ka-lee-grah-FEE.
Feminine: la bibliographie. The ph sounds like f, and the ending sounds like -FEE.

lessons.title: -ry → -rie / -oire · Nouns in -ry · 2
lessons.objective: -ory often becomes -oire: history → l'histoire, victory → la victoire. Other -ry words often end in -rie: industry → l'industrie.
lessons.explanation: Many -ry words differ: library → la bibliothèque, factory → l'usine. la mémoire is memory; un mémoire is a dissertation.
lessons.speakingPrompt: Say each French word without looking. Then compare it with the model voice.

items.note: Feminine: la gloire. The oi sounds like wa: GLWAHR. This is the -ory → -oire pattern.
Feminine: l'industrie. The ending is -rie, not -ry, and sounds like ree; the in is nasal.
Feminine: la théorie. The th is a plain t, and the ending sounds like ree: tay-oh-REE.

lessons.title: -or → -eur · Nouns in -or · 2
lessons.objective: -or usually becomes -eur, and people and machines are masculine: le docteur, l'acteur, le moteur.
lessons.explanation: Exceptions in gender: la couleur, l'erreur, la valeur. Most abstract -eur nouns are feminine.
lessons.speakingPrompt: Say each French word without looking. Then compare it with the model voice.

items.note: Feminine: la couleur, an exception to the masculine rule. -eur is close to the ur of English fur, with a back-of-throat r: koo-LUR.
Feminine: l'erreur, another exception. The double r is one sound at the back of the throat: eh-RUR.
Masculine: le professeur, used for women too (la professeure is also common). It also means teacher; prof is the short form.
